deep.reconstruction:
PURPOSE. This page turns the nested-radical expressions of the previous page into closed forms and 5-place numerical values for the sines of the odd multiples of omega = 90°/17 = pi/34. In effect these are the half-chords of the regular 17-gon and 34-gon. It is the trigonometric payoff of the Gaussian-period construction of the 17-gon.

LINK TO THE PREVIOUS PAGE. There Gauss wrote 8(2,n) for 8 times the two-term period zeta^n + zeta^{-n} = 2cos(2 pi n/17). So 8(2,n) = 16cos(2 pi n/17).

NOTATION (as on the page).
- a = sqrt(17)
- b = sqrt(34+2a), b' = sqrt(34-2a). These are the four-term-period radicals.
- c = 2 sqrt(17+3a+2b+b')
- c' = 2 sqrt(17+3a-2b-b')
- c'' = 2 sqrt(17-3a-b+2b')
- c''' = 2 sqrt(17-3a+b-2b')
- 17 omega = 90°.

CONVERSION TO SINES (my explanation of the implicit step).
- sin(k omega) = cos((17-k)omega) = cos(m pi/17), with m = (17-k)/2.
- So 16 sin(k omega) = 16cos(2 pi m/34). It reduces to one of the eight values 8(2,n), using n ≡ ±m or ±(17-m)/2 (mod 17) as appropriate.
- Example: sin omega = cos(8 pi/17) = cos(2 pi·4/17) = cos(2 pi·13/17). Hence 16 sin omega = 8(2,13) = -1+a+b'-c'.
- The list at lower right (1.8.8, 3.7.7, …, 15.1.1) records this index correspondence k -> m = (17-k)/2.

THE EIGHT FORMULAS.
- 16 sin omega = -1+a+b'-c'
- 16 sin 3omega = 1+a-b+c''
- 16 sin 5omega = -1-a+b+c''
- 16 sin 7omega = 1+a+b-c'''
- 16 sin 9omega = -1+a-b'+c
- 16 sin 11omega = 1+a+b+c'''
- 16 sin 13omega = -1+a+b'+c'
- 16 sin 15omega = 1-a+b'+c

NUMERICS. The constants are divided by 16:
- 1/16 = 0.06250
- a/16 = 0.25769
- b/16 = 0.40623
- b'/16 = 0.31717
- c/16 = 0.86099
- c'/16 = 0.42010
- c''/16 = 0.35970
- c'''/16 = 0.12379

These use the previous page's values sqrt17 = 4.1231056, b' = 5.0748191, b = 6.4997086, and inner roots 6.8879281, 3.3608155, 2.8776054, 0.9903300.

In each box Gauss adds the positive terms, adds the negative terms, and subtracts. For example, sin omega: 0.25769+0.31717 = 0.57486 and 0.06250+0.42010 = 0.48260, so sin omega = 0.09226. Results:
- sin omega = 0.09226
- sin 3omega = 0.27366
- sin 5omega = 0.44574
- sin 7omega = 0.60263
- sin 9omega = 0.73901
- sin 11omega = 0.85021
- sin 13omega = 0.93246
- sin 15omega = 0.98297

All agree with the true sin(k pi/34) to the last place, within one unit.

UPPER (ROTATED) NOTES AND SKETCH. These are rough geometric notes on points A–G with segment-product relations, apparently AC·AC = AB·BD = 4AB², AE·BE = AG·CG = AF·DF = AB², AF·EF = AB·AF. Together with the pencil triangles labelled 'cos', 'cos 8', '1 2 4', '9 8', they appear to explore a ruler-and-compass realisation via power-of-a-point relations, i.e. constructing roots of quadratics as products of segments. They are too fragmentary to reconstruct with certainty.
errors: The first value written for c''' (struck through, read as 0.06189) is half the correct value: the factor 2 in c''' = 2 sqrt(...) was forgotten. Gauss corrected it to 0.12379.
The values for b and b' were first entered swapped (0.31717 beside b, 0.40623 beside b'). Both were struck out and corrected.
In the sin omega box an intermediate (struck, ~0.6694) was miswritten and replaced by 0.57486.
No surviving errors: all eight final formulas and all eight numerical sines are correct to 5 decimals.

results.what: Explicit square-root expressions for sin(k pi/34), k = 1,3,…,15, i.e. cos(m pi/17) for m = 1..8, derived from the nested Gaussian periods of the 17th roots of unity
results.modern_name: Constructibility of the regular 17-gon; Gaussian periods / quadratic tower for Q(zeta_17)

results.what: Numerical evaluation of these radicals to 5 places as a check
Fragmentary segment-product relations for a geometric (ruler-and-compass) realisation
results.modern_name: Power-of-a-point construction of quadratic roots (cf. later 17-gon constructions by Richmond, Erchinger, etc.)
results.usually_credited_to: various; the Gauss-era construction of Erchinger (1825) was approved by Gauss

deep.surprise_reason: Explicit radical forms of the 17-gon sines are exactly Gauss's famous 1796 result. This page is a clean worked numerical verification, with no non-standard content.
